newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish SPOiF to trade Polish T-bills, NBP-bills.
newsitem.headline: Polish SPOiF to trade Polish T-bills, NBP-bills.

text.p: Polish bank-owned System Pozagieldowego Obrotu Instrumentami Finansowymi SA (SPOiF) will act as an intermediary in the Polish secondary T-bill and NBP-bill market from January 15, SPOiF deputy president said.

"This will be the first stage of SPOiF's activity, in which it will become an additional intermediary and competitor to brokers on the Polish secondary T-bill and NBP-bill markets," Janusz Lazarowicz told Reuters on Wednesday.

He told Reuters that banks connected by the company's electronic network will be able to automatically match bids with offers during daily sessions held from 0900 and 1430 local time, which should improve market liquidity.
All cash-transactions done by SPOiF on T-bills and NBP-bills will be settled through existing central bank's registers.
SPOiF, established in April 1996, now has 16 banks and Polish Banking Association as shareholders and a share capital of 1.625 million zlotys.
Lazarowicz said SPOiF would also want to organise derivative trade and hopes to launch it in three months.
He said the company planned to introduce a wide range of instruments based on T-bills, NBP-bills, interest rates and currencies.
The smallest T-bill contract would be 100,000 zlotys. The three- and six-month contracts on U.S. dollars and German marks would be 50,000 or 100,000 zlotys, Lazarowicz said.
He said SPOiF was working on its own interest rate index to use it for interest rate contracts rather than the existing Warsaw Interbank Offer Rate (WIBOR).
